text:
maya_research: Quick heads-up — ran end-to-end bench comparing SSE vs WebSocket for streaming and non-streaming endpoints across us-west1 (A100s) and eu-central1 (H100s). Attached heatmaps + short kernel notes.

brian_infra: Nice. What's the request mix? prompt len, concurrency?

maya_research: Mostly chat-like: avg prompt 120 tokens, response target 256 tokens, ~90% short-turn messages. Tested: non-stream HTTP (sync chunked), SSE, websocket streaming. Concurrency sweep: 16 / 32 / 64 / 128.

anna_ml: Can you drop the CSV snippet and quant configs? Also any quality diffs?

maya_research: CSV below. Quant configs: fp16 baseline, GPTQ int4 for 13b (llm.int4), and 8-bit dynamic as a middle ground. Also tried KV-cache pinning vs ephemeral. Quality: small regressions on 13b-int4 flagged. neo-7b-int4 looks clean.

benchbot: AUTOMATED-BENCHMARK: 1792004330
payload: {
  "models": ["redwood-neo-7b", "redwood-13b-quant"],
  "gpus": ["A100-40GB(us-west1)", "H100-80GB(eu-central1)"],
  "endpoints": ["non-stream", "sse", "websocket"],
  "concurrency_sweep": [16,32,64,128]
}
summary: On A100 medium conc (32-64) SSE reduced p95 by ~12% vs non-stream; WS gave best p50 at high conc due to socket reuse. H100 throughput higher overall; int4 on H100 had kernel fallbacks that increased p95 variance.

rory_kernel: Kernel note: A100 used fused-attn kernels with continuous batching; H100 ran flash-attn for fp16 but fell back to generic kernels for int4 (GPTQ) — that explains variance.

sasha_eval: Did you run the eval prompts? 13b-int4 had ~2-3% degradation on our conversational probe earlier.

maya_research: For neo-7b int4 no measurable regression on our chat eval. 13b-int4 shows minor LM loss increase on a handful of prompts; flagged a rollout hold for those buckets.

anna_ml: Paste the heatmap/throughput snippet here please.

maya_research: Pasting CSV snippet: 
```
endpoint,gpu,concurrency,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_sec
non-stream,A100,32,120,410,850
sse,A100,32,110,360,920
websocket,A100,32,105,340,980
non-stream,H100,32,95,300,1200
sse,H100,32,88,260,1350
websocket,H100,32,90,280,1280
```

brian_infra: H100 shows much better T/s; SSE increases throughput ~8-12% on H100 and ~6-9% on A100. Websocket often has best p50 but p95 slightly worse on H100 when int4 kernels fallback.

rory_kernel: There's a newer NV patch that enables quantized flash-attn on H100 for GPTQ int4. We should try that; it may remove the fallback and smooth p95.

sasha_eval: Rollout suggestion: A/B 10% on eu-central1 for 13b-int4, gate on our probe set and LM-loss + response-quality metrics.

maya_research: Capacity sizing note: treat streaming (SSE/WS) as higher-CPU and longer-lived sockets; autoscaler policy: allow higher max_concurrency per GPU for WS (~1.3x) and SSE (~1.2x) vs non-stream to reflect better batching. Also lower per-request GPU allocation for streaming since tokens are incremental.

anna_ml: Add regression alert: LM-loss >1.5% OR token-quality drift on our probe set. Also surface kernel-fallback alert in console.

benchbot: ARTIFACTS: /bench/1792004321/heatmaps.png, /bench/1792004321/throughput_p95.csv

maya_research: Next steps: rory to try kernel patch on staging H100; brian to rerun int4 + patch at conc 64/128; sasha to prepare eval probes and dashboards. I'll post results in a follow-up thread.

brian_infra: On it — kicking off reruns now.

rory_kernel: Queued kernel patch, ETA ~4h.

sasha_eval: Assembling probes and dashboards now.

anna_ml: Thanks all :rocket:
